solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rolled up inside: one sun top

indicators.note: the word inside tells us one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to roll up is to arrive, so rolled up means came
the Roman numeral for one is I
Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: Someone rolls up a garment and tucks it inside, one sunny-day top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolled up' looks like folding clothes, but here it means turned up or arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless undergarment worn on the upper body, a kind of top.

clue.text: Newspaper article supporting well-known figure?

definitions.meaning: a regular piece by one writer in a paper
a pillar holding up a statue, as with Nelson's in Trafalgar Square

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper feature and a pillar topped by a famous statue share this name.

clue.text: A second mother to ten strays

parts.note: mom is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: strays suggests the letters of ten wander out of place

explanation.surface: A second mother looks after ten wandering animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment and a second are both very short spans of time.

clue.text: Consequently rights — puts in order

parts.note: so means therefore or consequently
RTS is an abbreviation for rights

explanation.surface: As a result, someone rights things by arranging them properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to arrange or organise them.

clue.text: One who doesn't have, say, a spray to give the finishing touch

definitions.text: a spray to give the finishing touch

indicators.note: say signals that we go by how the word is pronounced

parts.note: a lacker would be someone who lacks something

explanation.surface: A person short of things is offered a spray for a final touch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard glossy coating, often sprayed, finishes woodwork or holds hair in place.

clue.text: He erased the mistake, little imp!

indicators.note: erased says the letters of He are rubbed out of what follows

parts.note: taken as written
a mistake is an error
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A man corrects his slip and scolds a mischievous child.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ERROR loses HE to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A naughty child is called a little terror, an informal idiom for a small troublemaker.

clue.text: A Caesarean — how could you!

parts.note: a phrase of Julius Caesar's, reproaching a friend who betrayed him

explanation.surface: Someone is outraged on hearing a birth will be by surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caesarean' suggests a surgical birth; here it means a quotation from Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's dying reproach to his friend Brutus, in Shakespeare's play, means 'you too'.

clue.text: Meets on trip; is not terribly taken

parts.note: a run is a short trip

indicators.note: terribly taken suggests the letters of is not are badly treated and jumbled

explanation.surface: A traveller says he is not badly affected by the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: In studies, he'd broken down genetic types

indicators.note: In places the jumbled letters inside the studies

parts.note: to read is to study

indicators.note: broken down suggests the letters of he'd falling apart and regrouping

explanation.surface: A researcher's studies collapse when analysing kinds of genes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger hair comes from a recessive gene, so people with it form a genetic group.

clue.text: Green wrench, though it's often blue

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
to rick is to wrench or sprain a joint

explanation.surface: A green spanner, though it is usually painted blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic five-line verses are frequently bawdy, and blue here means risqué or smutty.

clue.text: Stewed and ready to eat

definitions.meaning: fruit with its pits removed is prepared for eating

explanation.definitionFit: Both stewed and the answer are slang for drunk; fruit such as cherries are pitted before being served.

clue.text: Didn't take punch or port

definitions.meaning: passed over something and let it remain
a blow struck with the boxer's other hand
the nautical word for the side opposite starboard

explanation.definitionFit: The word means abandoned, a blow with that hand, and the nautical side opposite starboard.

clue.text: Not having clue, misspelled 'diminutive'

parts.note: minus means lacking or without

indicators.note: misspelled tells us the letters of clue are written in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A note complains that a crossword lacks a clue and someone has spelt a word wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: A sly joke: the word is famously misspelt with an I in the middle, and the clue says 'misspelled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean extremely small or tiny.

clue.text: As consort, be free to enter

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, as if walking in through a door

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: Someone is told that, as a royal partner, they may come in freely.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse, and a woman on her wedding day becomes one.

clue.text: Lap up nearly all and sound drunk

indicators.note: nearly all says the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to slurp is to lap up a drink noisily

explanation.surface: Someone guzzles nearly everything and begins to speak like a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Running words together indistinctly is what a drunk person does when speaking.

clue.text: With a lot to pack, moving home's horrible

indicators.note: moving suggests these letters shifting about into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving house with so much to pack is horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means disgusting or detestable, so horrible fits.

clue.text: Believed to have been eroded by time

parts.note: rusted means corroded or eaten away

explanation.surface: An old structure is thought to have worn away over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: To be trusted is to be believed or relied upon.

clue.text: Plant from Spain. Yippee, a flowering plant!

parts.note: olé is a Spanish cry of delight, hence the mention of Spain
the aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A Spaniard cheers at the sight of a blooming plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This shrub, also called wild olive, is a plant of southern Europe and Asia.

clue.text: That's torn it — caught playing in church. Sorry

indicators.note: caught means the church letters hold the jumbled letters within

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of torn it are played around with

explanation.surface: A child caught playing in church apologises after a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means feeling remorse, the state of being sorry.

clue.text: A number on parole misbehaved. May be caught and imprisoned

indicators.note: in an across answer, on places the number after the scrambled letters
misbehaved shows the letters of parole behaving badly and rearranging

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A prisoner out on parole reoffends and may be caught and jailed again.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a big cat being captured and caged in a zoo, not a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: This big cat is a wild animal that can be trapped and kept in a cage.

clue.text: Wednesday arranged a send off: wet in the early morning

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of Wednesday are reordered once the other words are taken away

explanation.surface: Plans for a farewell party on Wednesday, on a damp morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' says A SEND comes away; rearrange what is left of WEDNESDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass covered with morning moisture is described this way.

clue.text: Title that reverts

indicators.note: reverts says the word reads the same when turned backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A property document that returns to its former owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal document proving ownership, so title is a synonym.

clue.text: Solved half the clues, but cheated

definitions.meaning: completed the clues in one direction of a crossword grid

explanation.definitionFit: Literally finished the vertical clues; idiomatically, defrauded or swindled someone.

clue.text: Believe direction is wrong, to start with

indicators.note: is wrong suggests those letters are in the wrong order
to start with keeps only the opening part of the word direction

explanation.surface: Someone is certain the route is mistaken from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the start of 'direction', DIRECT, and rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to accept it as true.

clue.text: Price of daily, for instance, has risen

parts.note: a char or daily is a cleaning woman, an old British term

indicators.note: has risen means the letters climb upwards, read backwards in a down answer

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation meaning for example

explanation.surface: The cost of a daily newspaper, for example, has gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like a newspaper but is a cleaner, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price asked for goods or a service.

clue.text: Head for the hills, literally

parts.note: the first letter of the word hills is H, and this is how that letter is spelt out

explanation.surface: An instruction to flee to the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means run away; taken literally, the head of 'hills' is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the written name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, which begins hills.

clue.text: Double bed that allows you to keep your distance

definitions.text: Double bed that allows you to keep your distance

parts.words: Double bed that allows you to keep your distance
parts.note: a broad sleeping bunk, and also the idiom for avoiding someone

explanation.surface: A double bed roomy enough for a couple who prefer not to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a broad clearance is to keep well away; literally, it is a broad bunk.

clue.text: In a singer, ego is fundamental

indicators.note: In places the self inside the singer

parts.note: a bass is a singer with a deep voice
ego is Latin for I

explanation.surface: Within a vocalist, self-regard is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamental and a basis are both the underlying principle on which things rest.

clue.text: For the journey back, do stand

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: back tells us the word do is read backwards

explanation.surface: For the return journey, someone is told to stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a kind of stand.

clue.text: Think 'Drink' when son staggers in

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the drink

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

indicators.note: staggers suggests the letters of son lurching into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent thinks of drink when their boy comes home staggering.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to think about or ponder.

clue.text: Swam, putting fish in the shade!

indicators.note: in tells us the fish goes inside the colour

parts.note: red is a shade or colour
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone swims, placing a fish in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swam' is not swimming but a head swimming with dizziness.
explanation.definitionFit: When your head swam you felt giddy, and that is to have staggered or felt dizzy.

clue.text: I lay bet about it being an intoxicant

indicators.note: about means the stake goes around the other letters

parts.note: an ante is a stake or bet in poker
to lay is to set down

explanation.surface: A gambler places a wager on a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, an alcoholic drink that can intoxicate.
